Two of the tracker's open questions fit the Tice "driver" device: whether Ray Manta was a tool or complicit, and whether Larry and Cyril, the detectives "conveniently off sick", matter. The tracker hasn't changed since 2026-05-01, and the three finale outlines are still unfiled (memory/index.md). Each returning ally gives one piece of the timeline, and the piece that breaks the frame comes from a minor transport or bystander figure (Larry/Cyril or whoever moved the treasure to the trawler). ## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-10-09] Cooking's weekly recipe recommender is the only part of the wiki that decides what Fred actually eats, and it has never read Health. Health's main dementia source sets a food target that the 42 suggestions so far mostly miss.** [[health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026]] names B vitamins plus omega-3 as "the pair that matters", with targets of 2–4 g EPA+DHA a day and an Omega-3 Index above 8%. [[health/my-protocol]]'s Diet section is still "[to be added]", and [[cooking/cooking-overview]]'s Focus todo still lists "dietary approach" as undefined. Meanwhile [[cooking/recipe-suggestions]] has produced 42 dishes since 06-30. Only two are oily-fish mains: Grilled Mackerel (week of 07-20) and Seared Trout (week of 07-27). Nothing in the eleven weeks since has been oily fish. This week's Moules au Cidre is the first suggestion since July that hits both halves of the pair. Mussels are among the richest food sources of B12, with some EPA+DHA as well (general nutrition knowledge, not from a wiki source). That makes it a better fit for the Health page than anything the recommender has aimed for on purpose. **Why it matters:** the two empty pages could fill each other. Writing one line into my-protocol's Diet section (e.g. "oily fish or shellfish twice a week") would give the recommender a rule to follow, such as one omega-3 or B12 slot per weekly batch. Every Friday's batch would then double as the Health protocol in practice, instead of rotating the same three chefs with no goal.
